title: Hindi greetings and script
examples: How do I write my name in Devanagari?

explain.say: Today we learn how to greet people in Hindi.

items: You can use it with everyone.

explain.say: The word Namaste is very important for greetings.
The Devanagari script is used to write Hindi words.
We use different ways to speak to people.
If you greet a teacher, you should be formal.
In real life, you use greetings all the time.

items: Meet an elder: Say Namaste Sir

faq.a: It is a respectful greeting that means hello and goodbye. It is a gesture of respect when you say it.
asks: How do I say hello in Hindi?
What is the meaning of Namaste?

faq.q: Do I need to learn the Devanagari script?
faq.a: Learning the script helps you read Hindi words correctly. It is the writing system for Hindi.
asks: What alphabet do I use for Hindi?
How do I write Hindi words?

faq.q: When should I use a formal greeting?
faq.a: You use a formal greeting when speaking to people older than you or people you do not know well. This shows respect.
asks: Is it okay to be informal with teachers?
Who do I use formal greetings for?

faq.a: Yes, Namaste is a very common and safe greeting for almost everyone. It works in most situations.
asks: Is Namaste okay for all people?

faq.q: What is the difference between formal and informal?
faq.a: Formal language is polite and used in respectful settings. Informal language is casual and used with close friends.
asks: How do I know if I should be formal?

facts: Namaste is a common greeting in Hindi.
The Devanagari script is the writing system for Hindi.
Formal greetings show respect to elders or strangers.
Informal greetings are used among close friends.

quiz.say: You are greeting your school principal for the first time. Which greeting style is best?
quiz.why: Because the principal is an elder and you do not know them well, you must use a formal greeting to show respect.

wrong.0: This is too casual for someone you respect highly.
wrong.1: You are learning Hindi greetings, so you should try the Hindi way first.
wrong.2: Namaste is the standard and correct greeting word to use.

quiz.say: Your best friend greets you in the hallway. Which style of greeting is appropriate?
quiz.why: Since your friend is a close peer, a more casual or informal greeting is perfectly fine.

wrong.0: Using a very formal greeting with a friend sounds unnatural.
wrong.1: While Devanagari is the script, you need the spoken greeting first.
wrong.2: A greeting is always polite and expected when meeting someone.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes using Hindi greetings?

options.show: Always use the most formal greeting.
options.say: Always use the most formal greeting.

options.show: Use the same greeting for everyone.
options.say: Use the same greeting for everyone.

options.show: Use formal greetings for teachers and informal for classmates.
options.say: Use formal greetings for teachers and informal for classmates.

quiz.why: This shows you understand the difference between showing respect and being casual.

wrong.0: This can sound stiff when talking to people your own age.
wrong.1: Greetings are spoken words used in real-life conversations.
wrong.2: Language changes based on who you are talking to.
